significance.justification: Verified true, the claim would establish a form-(iii) predictive coupling and temporal ordering: a linearly decoded "harmfulness verdict" at the "</think> boundary" predicts prompt harmfulness better than visible CoT, and its answer-phase decay predicts later harmful output; the proposed re-assertion also adds a form-(ii) causal claim. This establishes a useful phenomenon and a coarse mechanism, but the labels weaken the conclusion: because the probe predicts whether the request is harmful, a "harmful latent verdict paired with a refusing output" is ordinarily correct recognition followed by refusal, not by itself a faked refusal, and no particular circuit or computational path is identified. Turpin et al. (2023), together with the 2025 study "Reasoning Models Don't Always Say What They Think," makes latent-versus-verbalized monitoring a concrete unresolved issue; a negative result would distinctly rule out this linear boundary signal as superior to text in explicit-thinking models, although it would not rule out nonlinear or differently timed verdicts, and "frequently overridden" lacks a threshold. In the topic-substitution check, generic mechanistic work on LLM safety would merit below 5; the above-median score comes specifically from the claimed cross-signal predictive ordering and pre-answer override trajectory.

reach.justification: The principal handle is a "threshold detector on the </think> verdict projection," supplemented by an intervention that "re-asserts the latent verdict at the answer boundary"; the detector is ex ante because the claim says it is "available before the answer is generated," leaving an action window for gating or intervention. Re-extraction would not transfer the exact direction, but the substantive claim predicts that newly extracted boundary scores will outperform CoT-text monitoring and exhibit verdict decay before overrides, so part of the conclusion transfers as a relation rather than merely as a search procedure. Its asserted scope is reasoning LLMs with explicit thinking blocks, with hidden-CoT and frontier models explicitly unestablished; downstream users could include safety auditors and deployment gatekeepers, although the questionable definition of "faked refusals" limits how directly they could act on every flagged cell. Under topic substitution, generic interpretability for safety would not earn this score; reach above the topic median is supported specifically by the quoted pre-answer detector and its usable lead time.
